da-vacuous.evidence: q-casimir-unique.lean:67-86: the theorem `unique_up_to_scalar` is a one-line projection of `unique_up_to_scalar_axiom`. The axiom takes only a centrality hypothesis `_hC` (named with underscore = unused) and asserts the scalar-equivalence conclusion directly.
da-vacuous.notes: Not vacuous in the `: True` sense — it is an honestly-declared external axiom (Kassel VI.4.9) with the real proposition as its conclusion, and the .md flags it as axiomatized standard quantum-group result. But the 'theorem' adds zero deductive content over the axiom; the centrality hypothesis is never used to derive anything (it is consumed wholesale by the axiom). This is the permitted 'axiomatize a standard external result' pattern, hence warn not fail.

da-overclaim.evidence: q-casimir-unique.lean:53-71 axiomatizes the entire uniqueness claim; the .md title/body present it as a 'proposition' with a proof block (q-casimir-unique-proof.md). The actual Lean content is `axiom`, not a derivation.
da-overclaim.notes: The .md is honest ('It is axiomatized here', 'no novel mathematical argument is claimed'), so this is not a hidden overclaim. The narrative proof block (Joseph-Letzter centre argument) is a sketch, not formalized. Minor: a reader sees a 'proposition' + 'proof' but Lean carries an axiom. Accurately scoped in prose, hence warn.

da-non-sequitur.evidence: q-casimir-unique-proof.md:7-13: 'Fixing the eigenvalue on V_j to be [j]_q[j+1]_q ... pins down b=1 and a=0' — the b=1 step is asserted, not shown. The centre is R[C_q], so a general central element is a polynomial p(C_q); the proof restricts to linear a+bC_q without justifying why the eigenvalue normalization forbids higher-degree central elements with the same V_j spectrum.
da-non-sequitur.notes: The .md proposition statement itself restricts to the form `FE + φ(K,K⁻¹)` (degree ≤ 1 in C_q), so the linear restriction is a hypothesis, not a gap, for the stated proposition. The proof block's 'b=1' pin is plausible (leading coefficient matching) but stated without the explicit eigenvalue-matching computation. Minor logical gap in the narrative sketch only.

da-lean-narrative-divergence.evidence: .md:1-5 claims uniqueness for central elements 'of the form FE + φ(K,K⁻¹) ... whose eigenvalue on the spin-j irrep is [j]_q[j+1]_q'. The Lean axiom `unique_up_to_scalar_axiom` (lean:67-71) hypothesizes ONLY centrality (`∀ a, C*a = a*C`); the eigenvalue-normalization condition and the `FE + φ(K,K⁻¹)` form restriction are NOT encoded as hypotheses.
da-lean-narrative-divergence.notes: Without the eigenvalue/form hypotheses the Lean claim is literally FALSE as a faithful encoding — two arbitrary central elements of U_q(su2) need NOT differ by a scalar (the centre is a full polynomial ring R[C_q], so C_q and C_q² are both central and do not differ by a scalar). The Lean docstring acknowledges 'carries the same spin-j eigenvalue normalisation' but the `axiom` signature drops that hypothesis, making the axiom as-stated over-strong / false. Since it is an opaque external axiom (no proof to verify against), severity is bounded to minor here, but this is a genuine .md-vs-Lean divergence: the Lean omits the two hypotheses that make the narrative claim true.

da-citation-misuse.notes: Kassel §VI.4.9 (Joseph-Letzter centre, Z(U_q(sl2)) = R[C_q]) is correctly invoked for the up-to-scalar uniqueness.

da-definitional-ambiguity.evidence: .md:3 'φ(K,K⁻¹) (Laurent polynomial in K)' — the admissible degree of φ is unbounded, yet the uniqueness argument (q-casimir-unique-proof.md) treats the element as linear-in-C_q. The mapping between 'Laurent polynomial in K' and 'linear in C_q' is not stated.
da-definitional-ambiguity.notes: C_q = FE + (qK + q⁻¹K⁻¹ - 2)/(q-q⁻¹)² (standard), so 'FE + φ(K)' with φ a degree-1 Laurent poly is exactly linear-in-C_q only for that specific φ; a higher-degree φ(K) need not be central. The class of elements the proposition quantifies over is mildly ambiguous. Minor.

da-referee-verdict.notes: verdict: accept-with-minor-revisions. referee_argument: The block honestly axiomatizes a standard quantum-group result (Joseph-Letzter centre, Kassel VI.4.9) and the .md is candid that no novel argument is claimed. The one substantive objection is da-lean-narrative-divergence: the Lean `axiom QCasimir.unique_up_to_scalar_axiom` hypothesizes only centrality and DROPS both the eigenvalue-normalization and the `FE+φ(K)` form restriction that the .md statement carries — so the axiom as written is over-strong (two arbitrary central elements of U_q(su2) do not differ by a scalar, since the centre is the full polynomial ring R[C_q]). The axiom should carry the eigenvalue-normalization hypothesis to faithfully encode the narrative. Otherwise sound.
